## Purpose
This document examines population growth, PSP/MSA spatial boundaries and long-term urban expansion across Melbourne's fringe growth areas.

## Packages
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(terra)
```

## Data
```{r}
population <- read_csv(
  "../data/meeting1/abs_erp_population_2001_2025.csv"
)

msa <- read_csv(
  "../data/meeting1/msa_precinct_attributes.csv"
)

lga_boundary <- st_read(
  "../data/LGA_2025_AUST_GDA2020/LGA_2025_AUST_GDA2020.shp",
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Create study LGAs
study_lga <- lga_boundary |>
  filter(LGA_NAME25 %in% c(
    "Casey", "Hume", "Melton", "Whittlesea", "Wyndham"
  ))
```


## Population growth
```{r}
population_growth <- population |>
  filter(year %in% c(2001, 2025)) |>
  select(council, year, population) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year,
    values_from = population
  ) |>
  mutate(
    growth = `2025` - `2001`,
    growth_percent = growth / `2001` * 100
  )

population_growth
```
Population growth provides broader context for increasing development pressure across the five fringe LGAs.

## PSP/MSA spatial processing
```{r}
# PSP boundary
psp_boundary <- st_read(
  "../data/PSP_Boundary/PSP_Boundary.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Check unmatched PSP names
anti_join(
  msa |> distinct(psp_name),
  psp_boundary |> st_drop_geometry() |> distinct(PSP_NAME),
  by = c("psp_name" = "PSP_NAME")
)

anti_join(
  psp_boundary |> st_drop_geometry() |> distinct(PSP_NAME),
  msa |> distinct(psp_name),
  by = c("PSP_NAME" = "psp_name")
)

# Standardise PSP names
psp_boundary <- psp_boundary |>
  mutate(
    PSP_NAME = case_when(
      PSP_NAME == "Quandong PSP (Council-led)" ~ "Quandong PSP",
      PSP_NAME == "Croskell" ~ "Croskell (Casey Central)",
      TRUE ~ PSP_NAME
    )
  )

# Join MSA attributes to PSP boundary
msa_spatial <- msa |>
  left_join(
    psp_boundary,
    by = c("psp_name" = "PSP_NAME")
  ) |>
  st_as_sf()

# Check unmatched MSA precincts
msa_spatial |>
  filter(st_is_empty(geometry)) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(psp_name, lga, subregion, type)
```
Of the 122 MSA records, 117 were successfully matched to PSP polygons after standardising two inconsistent precinct names. Five precincts remain unmatched.

## Urban expansion analysis
```{r}
# Land Cover Time Series
landcover_files <- list.files(
  "../data/VIC_LANDCOVER_TS",
  pattern = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

periods <- c(
  "1985-90", "1990-95", "1995-00", "2000-05",
  "2005-10", "2010-15", "2015-19"
)

study_lga_vicgrid <- st_transform(study_lga, 3111)
```

```{r}
# Calculate urban area by LGA
get_urban_area <- function(file, period) {

  landcover <- rast(file)

  landcover_study <- crop(
    landcover,
    vect(study_lga_vicgrid)
  ) |>
    mask(vect(study_lga_vicgrid))

# Built environment and urban area
  urban <- landcover_study %in% c(1, 2)

  urban_lga <- extract(
    urban,
    vect(study_lga_vicgrid),
    fun = sum,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

# Each 25 m x 25 m cell equals 0.0625 hectares
  study_lga_vicgrid |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    select(LGA_NAME25) |>
    bind_cols(urban_lga) |>
    select(-ID) |>
    rename(urban_cells = 2) |>
    mutate(
      period = period,
      urban_area_ha = urban_cells * 0.0625
    )
}

urban_change <- map2_dfr(
  landcover_files,
  periods,
  get_urban_area
)

urban_change
```

```{r}
# Urban expansion
urban_growth <- urban_change |>
  filter(period %in% c("1985-90", "2015-19")) |>
  select(LGA_NAME25, period, urban_area_ha) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = period,
    values_from = urban_area_ha
  ) |>
  mutate(
    growth_ha = `2015-19` - `1985-90`,
    growth_percent = growth_ha / `1985-90` * 100
  )

urban_growth
```
Urban land increased across all five study LGAs. Casey had the largest absolute increase, while Melton had the largest proportional increase.

```{r}
# Urban land trend
ggplot(
  urban_change,
  aes(
    x = period,
    y = urban_area_ha,
    group = LGA_NAME25,
    colour = LGA_NAME25
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Urban land area over time",
    x = "Period",
    y = "Urban area (ha)",
    colour = "LGA"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
